correctness.rationale: An infinite Bernoulli-bit model follows from dyadic equidistribution; the carry count equals h minus the digit-sum change, and runs of length at most h terminate before the next 1 of the shift. Each weak composition of j<=h into h geometric run lengths has probability 2^{-(h+j)}, yielding the exact profile and central-binomial tail. Exact finite-state and dyadic enumerations returned VERIFY_OK; neither is substituted for the analytic argument. Boundary gap two h=2 fails as expected.

value.rationale: Cusick digit-sum bias at a prescribed binary Hamming weight is an actively researched quantity. This result gives a complete infinite exact density profile for all sufficiently separated 1-bit shifts of arbitrary weight, rather than another general non-sharp bound or numerical list, and identifies an explicit h^{-1/2} bias regime sharply distinct from known fixed-weight minimum-bias asymptotics. The spacing threshold has a concrete counterexample at weight two if reduced. It offers a closed-form benchmark and clarifies which carry interactions prevent position invariance.
